overall: Strong draft: all 232 items pass the checker (ok_rate 1.0), all 78 pool tokens are covered, and the writer consistently avoided the obvious Irish uses (Samuel Beckett, James Joyce, Oscar Wilde, Roy Keane, St Patrick, Cork/Galway/Limerick as places, the sport hurling). Facts I checked are correct; the 9 exclusive calls (anair, Bord, Donegal, Dublin x2, riscoll, Ryanair, Sinn, Valera) are right (Spanair, Bordeaux, Driscoll tokenize away or are obscure). Main issues: (1) the no-space 'Ireland' token should be exclusive: it is the concept's own name and the items rely on the contrived 'N.Ireland'; (2) a few spellings exist only to force a token ('Sir Alec (Guinness)', 'Scots Irish', 'Óðinn', 'Santa Fé'); natural alternatives exist for inness (McGuinness, quoted 'Guinness World Records') and Irish (Scots-Irish goes to the no-space token); (3) some items give an Ireland-knower an edge (Bally- place prefix, Ulster Rugby, the whisky / 'uisce beatha' etymology); (4) near-duplicates (Garda x2 Italy, € 'before the euro' x2, Fátima shrine x2, Eich x2) and one fact duplicated across tokens (Kilmer's 'Trees' under ' Joyce' and ' Kil').
